note: Facts only from each model's own repo/model card and jevbench adapter docs, read 2026-09-20. Fields set to null are unknown; do not invent them.

models.name: Jev
how: Sends the state and typed questions to the hosted /v1/systemone endpoint and returns a probability for every option.
Internals are not published, so this page can only describe its interface and measured behaviour.
models.price: $0.042 per million input tokens, output free (public tariff); about 950 input tokens per decision in JevBench
models.sauce: Not published. Only the interface is known: state and typed questions go in, a probability for every option comes out.

models.name: SemIf (formerly OpenJev)
models.architecture: Decoder-only LLM used as a classifier
how: Each option is given an answer letter and a description.
One forward pass, no text generation: the model's logits for the declared answer letters are read directly and passed through a softmax.
The base model is not fine-tuned. Score questions are not part of the author's own method; JevBench maps them to the same letter scheme.
models.sauce: No training at all. Label the options A, B, C, run a frozen LLM once, and read how strongly it wants to write each letter next.

models.name: Cygnet
models.licence: Shim MIT; weights Apache-2.0 with Google's Gemma Prohibited Use Policy
models.architecture: Decoder-only LLM used as a classifier
how: Each option is shown as a letter with its criteria text kept verbatim.
One vLLM request with one output token: the model's own probability for each option letter at the answer position is read, then renormalised over the options.
One calibration temperature (3.4) is applied. It was fitted on the authors' own generated items, not on JevBench's public set. The weights are not fine-tuned.
models.served_as: HTTP, vLLM plus shim, GPU (bf16, 16384-token limit)
models.sauce: No training at all. Label the options A, B, C, run frozen Gemma 4 12B once, read how strongly it wants to write each letter, and soften with one temperature.

models.name: Winnow-12B (Q8)
models.base: Gemma 4 12B IT, LoRA rank 32 merged into the weights (Q8_0 GGUF, 12.67 GB)
models.architecture: Decoder-only LLM with native typed-decision serving
how: The model sees a letter-labelled question. The server picks verified single-token labels, reads their logits and normalises over those candidates (a softmax over the logits).
Serves noul, choice and score questions natively through a patched llama.cpp server (winnow-inference), with batches of questions run in waves.
Also offers /v1/chat/completions, and image input when the 175 MB mmproj projector is loaded.
models.served_as: HTTP, llama.cpp CUDA, Q8_0 GGUF, 65536-token context
models.sauce: A Gemma 4 12B fine-tune served by a purpose-built llama.cpp build: label the options with letters, read the label logits once, softmax over them.

models.name: open-alternative-jev
models.architecture: Decoder-only LLM used as a classifier
how: Reads the model's logits over the answer options in a single forward pass; nothing is generated.
Run in the author's recommended "separate" mode, where each question is scored on its own.
Sensitive to option order: JevBench measured 21% versus 72% on answer-judging items when the options were reversed.
models.sauce: The same letter-logit idea on a frozen LLM, scoring each question on its own. It is sensitive to the order of the options.

models.name: kev 4B
models.architecture: Hybrid (Gated DeltaNet) decoder with pointer readout
how: A LoRA-tuned causal LM is run prefill-only: no generation.
A pointer head reads hidden states at option-boundary tokens and scores each option.
On attention-only bases the questions share one state prefix behind a block-causal mask; hybrid Qwen3.5 backbones use one causal row per question instead.
models.sauce: A small learned pointer head, plus LoRA tuning of the LLM, teaches the model to point at the right option's boundary token.

models.name: kev 0.8B
models.architecture: Hybrid (Gated DeltaNet) decoder with pointer readout
how: Same recipe as kev 4B on a smaller backbone.
LoRA-tuned causal LM, prefill-only, with a pointer head over option-boundary tokens.
models.sauce: The same pointer-head recipe on a smaller backbone; hybrid layers mean each question is read as its own row.

models.name: kev 0.5B (prototype)
how: The original prototype and the only kev here on an attention-only backbone, so it uses the packed block-causal mask.
Trained with log loss on converted public datasets (Banking77, BoolQ, AG News, MNLI, SST-5, Yelp). The author marks it superseded.
models.sauce: The one attention-only kev, so several questions can share the state in one pass while a block-causal mask keeps them apart.

models.name: jeff
models.licence: MIT code; GLiFormer weights per their model card
how: An encoder reads the state together with the question and options in one pass.
Option scores are normalised sigmoids, temperature-scaled by 3.2.
Yes/no questions get their own encoder pass; choice and score questions share one unless isolation is set to all.
A micro-batcher groups concurrent requests for the GPU.
models.sauce: An encoder reads the state, question and options together in both directions, then scores each option with a sigmoid, temperature-scaled by 3.2.

models.name: Laya
how: A ModernBERT-large encoder reads the state and inserts a marker before each option.
The head returns a softmax over the option markers, which is the model's own distribution.
The documented budget is 512 tokens per question; longer states are truncated by the package.
models.sauce: A marker is placed before every option; a head reads the encoder's output at each marker and takes a softmax over them.

models.name: openJev Verdict
models.architecture: Encoder classifier with an abstention slot
how: One forward pass returns probabilities over the options plus an abstention slot.
JevBench drops the abstention mass and renormalises, the author's own rule for yes/no questions.
Run on CPU in this benchmark, so its latency is not comparable to the GPU models.
models.sauce: Adds an abstention slot, so the model can say the evidence is insufficient. The benchmark drops that slot and renormalises.

models.name: Clef Flash
models.architecture: Decoder backbone with a joint schema head
models.sauce: A small transformer head reads the backbone's final hidden states, routes evidence from the state to each question, and scores every option of every question jointly in one forward pass.
how: The Qwen3.5-9B backbone reads the state (text, JSON, images or video) once.
A joint schema head routes evidence from the state to each question and returns one logit per allowed option.
A softmax per question gives the probabilities; there is no generation and no output parsing.
The card says it was tested on a single H200; the larger sibling is Clef (not yet added).
Takes images as well as text; the card also documents video, which we have not tested. Questions in one request are decided jointly.

models.name: Clef Flash Q4
models.architecture: Decoder backbone with a joint schema head
models.served_as: llama.cpp server b11430, local GPU (text and images)
models.sauce: The same Clef Flash model with its backbone quantized to 4 bits (Q4_K_M) by a third party. The decision head is kept at Q8_0, per the quantizer's card. Not made or tested by Cloudflare.
how: Same mechanism as Clef Flash: one forward pass, one logit per option, a softmax per question.
The quantizer's card says the decision head is stored at Q8_0 in every quantized file, and that no importance matrix was used.
Images work through a separate 0.92 GB vision projector (--mmproj); the Image Lab results use it. Video is not tested.
Run to find how far the model can be shrunk before accuracy drops; compare it with the full-precision Clef Flash.

models.name: Clef Flash Q2
models.architecture: Decoder backbone with a joint schema head
models.served_as: llama.cpp server b11430, local GPU (text only here)
models.sauce: The same Clef Flash model with its backbone quantized to Q2_K by a third party. The decision head is kept at Q8_0, per the quantizer's card, and no importance matrix was used (the quantizer says that is not possible for a decision model), so the quantizer warns of a larger quality loss than usual. Not made or tested by Cloudflare.
how: Same mechanism as Clef Flash: one forward pass, one logit per option, a softmax per question.
Q2_K is a mixed quantization: 4.19 GB for 9.08B parameters is about 3.7 bits per weight on average, not 2. Our Q4_K_M is about 5.3.
The quantizer's card says the decision head is stored at Q8_0 in every quantized file, and that no importance matrix was used.
Text only here: the vision projector was not loaded for this copy. Run to find how far the model can be shrunk before world-knowledge accuracy drops.

tiers.label: Original
tiers.note: The 72-decision cohort published with JevBench v1.

tiers.label: Hard
tiers.note: Reasoning-heavy decisions written and cross-reviewed by two frontier models before any system ran.

code_rule: Family letters plus size. B = billions of parameters, H = hundreds of millions (KEV8H is 0.8B, VERD2H is 151M). Jev's size isn't publicly disclosed, so its code is just JEV -- no digits, since nothing else uses that prefix. Codes are at most six characters and appear in the same form on every page.
